title: Byte-Framed Cache Protocol Parser
prompt:
Implement `process_protocol(data: bytes) -> bytes`, a single-connection in-memory cache protocol interpreter. The input may contain several commands back to back. Command headers are ASCII and end in `
`; values are arbitrary bytes. A key is a nonempty ASCII string matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`. Malformed frames must raise `ValueError`.

Supported requests:

- `set KEY SIZE
PAYLOAD
` stores exactly `SIZE` bytes of payload and appends `STORED
` to the response. The byte after the payload must be the required terminating newline, even when the payload contains newlines or null bytes. A later set for the same key replaces its value.
- `get KEY [KEY ...]
` appends one `VALUE KEY SIZE
PAYLOAD
` block for every requested key that exists, in request order. Repeated requested keys produce repeated blocks. Then append exactly one `END
` for that get request.

`SIZE` is a non-negative base-10 integer. Parse with a byte cursor rather than splitting the whole stream by line, because payload bytes are not line-framed. Use only the standard library.

example.reasoning: Only stored keys produce VALUE blocks, and each get ends with one END marker.
